results.evidence: Two statute references appear: 18 U.S.C. § 2244 (real federal abusive sexual contact statute, correctly scoped to federal jurisdiction) and Federal Rule of Evidence 412 (real rape shield rule). All other legal descriptions use general language with jurisdiction qualifiers.
No individual attorney or legal scholar names appear. The post refers only to generic roles ('defense attorneys', 'your attorney', 'SANE nurses', 'independent forensic expert').

No specific percentages, counts, or rates appear without sources. Factual claims use general phrasing throughout: 'similar rates', 'only a minority', 'the overwhelming majority', 'commonly cost tens of thousands' with a qualifying parenthetical.

Procedural claims are jurisdiction-qualified ('in most jurisdictions', 'depending on the state', 'many states allow') or describe genuinely universal requirements (rape shield motions require pretrial filing in all U.S. jurisdictions, burden of proof is beyond a reasonable doubt in all criminal cases).
Only 'Miranda warnings' appears, which is on the approved exceptions list as universally known legal terminology functioning as a legal concept rather than a case citation.

Registration consequences are attributed to SORNA with specific tier descriptions. Other collateral consequences are qualified: 'Arrest records are generally public in most jurisdictions', 'many states allow expungement', penalties stated with 'depending on the jurisdiction and degree'.
